definition: LMX theory is a relationship-focused perspective that looks at the quality of the exchange between a leader or teacher and a member or student. In this study context, it is used to explain how stronger or weaker relationships can change how people weigh risk and act on feedback-seeking.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define LMX theory as a “relationship-focused perspective” or describe it as examining “the quality of the exchange” between a leader/teacher and a member/student.

The packet supports that “student-LMX” moderates effects involving perceived risk and perceived benefit on feedback seeking, but it does not support the definition’s framing that this is what LMX theory itself is “used to explain” in general terms; the packet presents LMX theory as the basis for a study hypothesis/boundary condition rather than a general definition of the theory.

The definition adds an unsupported generalization that LMX theory concerns exchange quality between a “leader or teacher” and a “member or student”; the packet only supports student-LMX in a higher-education setting and does not define the theory that broadly.

The study context is only partly supported: the packet says LMX moderated the risk pathway in feedback seeking, but it does not support the broader claim that stronger or weaker relationships generally change how people weigh risk and act on feedback-seeking.
